column1: Supplier selection criteria, weights and scoring scales
Weights are inputs (blue). They feed the WPM sheet. Basis: Evidence = scored today from public sources; RFQ = scored when the written quotation arrives.

column6: Scoring scale (1-5)
column7: Why it matters for PROBOCA

column6: FOB price vs the Comex Stat 2026 FOB benchmark: 5 = 5% or more below; 4 = 0-5% below; 3 = 0-3% above; 2 = 3-6% above; 1 = more than 6% above or no quote. The CFR price feeds the landed-cost model
column7: Landed cost is the largest block of PROBOCA's rubric (25%) and the only reason to buy Brazilian breast instead of US breast that enters duty-free under USMCA.

column6: 5 = letter of credit at sight or documents against payment; 4 = 30% advance or less; 3 = 50% advance; 2 = more than 50% advance; 1 = 100% advance
column7: Brazilian cargo spends about 30 days at sea, so terms set the working capital tied up per container; full prepayment to a new supplier is the classic fraud pattern.

column6: 5 = firm price valid 15 days or more, or a formula on a public index; 3 = valid 7 days; 1 = indicative price only
column7: PROBOCA chooses between spot, formula and forward prices; a purchasing committee can only act on a dated, firm quote.

column6: 5 = one container, calibres can be mixed; 3 = two or three containers; 1 = five or more, or fixed program only
column7: First orders are trial loads, and PROBOCA buys part of its volume spot (about 30% in turkey); a high minimum blocks the trial.

column6: 5 = accepts a duty reopener and shares the duty risk; 3 = accepts renegotiation only; 1 = rejects
column7: Duty-free access for Brazilian chicken ends on December 31, 2026 unless the decree is renewed; without it the duty is 75%.

column3: SENASICA eligibility of the shipping plant (gate)
column6: 5 = shipping plant on SENASICA's list with deboning authorized; 1 = not on the list (disqualifies the offer)
column7: Product from a plant that is not on the list cannot enter Mexico, whatever the price; PROBOCA asks for the plant on the SENASICA list, not just a big company.

column6: 5 = BRCGS, IFS or FSSC 22000 confirmed by the company; 4 = reported in an older or secondary source, or certifications claimed without naming the scheme; 3 = not found; 1 = none
column7: PROBOCA holds SQF and FSSC certification and processes product for large food brands; an uncertified raw-material supplier weakens that certified system.

column6: 5 = meets the spec sheet, including calibre range and defect tolerances; 3 = partial; 1 = does not meet it
column7: The 2025 teams quoted product families instead of one SKU; the specification is what the receiving plant inspects.

column6: 5 = verified clean record; 4 = no major incident found in public sources; 3 = past incident at a plant or a group-level case; 2 = food-safety fraud case at company level; 1 = active ban
column7: A shipment is only as reliable as the certificates behind it; integrity failures have closed whole markets to Brazilian plants.

column6: Share of authorized plants outside Rio Grande do Sul, the state with the 2025 commercial avian-flu outbreak and a 2026 backyard case: 5 = 100%; 4 = 75% or more; 3 = 50-74%; 2 = below 50%
column7: Mexico closes imports by state: in June 2025 it kept only Rio Grande do Sul closed.

column6: 5 = 1 million birds per day or more; 4 = 500,000 to 1 million; 3 = 300,000 to 500,000; 2 = 100,000 to 300,000; 1 = below 100,000
column7: Scale is the first sign that a supplier can sustain a weekly container program through the year.

column3: Supply continuity: authorized plants and states
column6: 5 = five or more authorized deboning plants in three or more states; 4 = four or more plants, or two states; 3 = three plants; 2 = two plants; 1 = one plant
column7: A second authorized plant, ideally in another state, keeps supply running if one plant or one state is closed.

column6: 5 = 14 days or less from purchase order to sailing, weekly sailings; 3 = 15-25 days; 1 = more than 25 days
column7: Transit to Altamira is already 30 days, and the duty that applies is the one in force on the day the vessel anchors.
column8: Supplier quotation; Maersk (n.d.); Ley Aduanera, art. 56

column6: 5 = verified recurrent shipments to Mexico; 4 = Mexico listed as a market on official channels; 3 = eligible plants but no public evidence; 1 = none
column7: Errors in the sanitary certificate or labels cause holds at Altamira; an exporter that already ships to Mexico has the documents right.

column3: Responsiveness and completeness of the RFQ answer
column6: 5 = complete answer in 3 business days or less; 3 = within 7 days or partial; 1 = no answer
column7: How a supplier answers a quotation request predicts how it will handle claims and after-sales problems.

column6: 5 = public policy with audits of 100% of units; 4 = public policy or commitment and reporting; 3 = farm certification or mention in a report; 2 = no public information; 1 = documented violations
column7: Protein producers are now ranked on animal welfare by investor initiatives such as FAIRR; a buyer can only pass that assurance on if its supplier has it.

column6: 5 = third-party rating such as CDP plus quantified results; 4 = GRI report with quantified results; 3 = GRI-aligned report, or extensive reporting with unresolved controversies; 2 = no report found; 1 = documented violations
column7: Deforestation-linked feed, water use and emissions are reputational and regulatory risks; CDP and GRI reporting let a buyer verify them.
column8: Company reports; O Presente Rural (2024, 2026); Portal Palotina (2025)

column6: 5 = farmer-owned cooperative that distributes its surplus and runs social programs; 3 = corporate integrator with published labor or social policies; 2 = limited disclosure; 1 = documented labor abuses
column7: No Fairtrade standard exists for poultry; cooperative ownership is the closest equivalent because value returns to the farming families.
column8: Company reports; C.Vale (2026); Gazeta Regional (2026); Feedfood (2026)

column6: 5 = revenue of R$20 billion or more, or a listed group; 4 = R$5-20 billion; 3 = R$1-5 billion; 2 = below R$1 billion; 1 = financial distress
column7: A supplier has to survive a 12-24 month relationship and be able to absorb claims and replace rejected loads.
